subject: Hosted API commit: tier amplification, rate-floor and invoicing cadence
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@vertexlabs.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: Ava Rios <ava.rios@vertexlabs.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit: tier amplification, rate-floor and invoicing cadence

I reviewed the latest proposal (thanks for the quick turnaround). Two things from my side: first, the recommended monthly commit of 3.5M tokens is acceptable — that aligns with our Q4 forecast — but we need clarity on what happens if we breach the soft-burst for two consecutive months. Second, billing cadence: our finance team prefers net-45 invoices for committed tiers, otherwise we need a PO-based up-front for larger commits. Can you confirm whether Redwood can sign net-45 for VertexLabs on a one-year renewal?

Also attaching the internal usage forecast for October-November for context.

—Sam
Head of Platform, VertexLabs
From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@vertexlabs.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, Ava Rios <ava.rios@vertexlabs.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit: tier amplification, rate-floor and invoicing cadence

Hi Sam — thanks for the quick read and the forecast. Short answers up front: 1) soft-burst behavior: our standard is a graduated overage band with a 15% cushion month-to-month and an automatic fall-back to the prior committed tier if breaches persist for 2 full consecutive billing periods unless we agree to a committed uplift. We can document an explicit grace/containment clause in the SOW. 2) net-45: I can escalate that to finance — our standard is net-30 but we have flexibility on enterprise renewals with a one-year term and a signed PO. I'll loop in Karthik and Marissa to confirm the commercial and invoicing paperwork.

Proposed next steps: (a) Karthik to confirm updated pricing table with a 3.5M monthly commit and a soft-burst band, (b) Marissa to prepare an SOW addendum that includes the grace clause and the billing cadence options, (c) I’ll follow up with your finance contact to confirm PO timing. Can we target a sign-off by end of next week?

Thanks,
Irene
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@vertexlabs.com>, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-28T13:27:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing and commit mechanics for VertexLabs renewal

Sam / team — adding the commercial detail Irene asked for. High level: we can do the 3.5M token monthly committed tier at the following unit economics: committed rate = $0.0008/token for hosted generation, overage tier up to 15% at $0.0011/token, and any sustained month >115% for two consecutive months will trigger either (a) an automatic uplift to the next committed tier (with pro-rata billing for that month) or (b) adherence to the prior committed rate with a one-time remediation credit if the customer supplies a short-term spike justification. We prefer option (a) for predictability but will make (b) available if VertexLabs needs time to finalize capacity planning.

Invoice cadence: we can accept net-45 on a one-year contract with a signed PO and credit-review (standard enterprise practice). We will include language in the SOW that allows for PO-based prepayment if finance needs it.

I’ve uploaded a refreshed pricing_table_q3.csv and a versioned SOW draft to the shared Drive link Irene included. Marissa — can you add the grace clause and the invoicing options to the SOW and send a tracked document to Sam?

—Karthik
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@vertexlabs.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-29T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: SOW addendum and invoice term options (VertexLabs)

Hi Sam — I uploaded SOW-hosted-commit-draft.docx to the Drive and included tracked changes in the attached PDF. Key additions I put in:
- A 2-month consecutive breach flow that triggers an automatic tier uplift unless both parties agree to an exception in writing (exception window: 30 days).
- A 15% soft-burst band applied to monthly committed tokens with overage pricing tier as Karthik noted.
- Billing: primary option = net-45 with signed PO and credit check. Alternate = quarterly prepay if VertexLabs decides to avoid PO timing risk.
- A 30-day review clause where Redwood will provide a one-time usage audit and recommended optimization settings (batching/kv-cache) if VertexLabs triggers >130% usage in any single month.

Can you confirm that net-45 + PO works for your team, Sam? If so I’ll produce a final clean SOW and circulate for signatures. If not, please tell me which of the alternate paths you prefer.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Contracts Manager — Redwood Inference
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@vertexlabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-30T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOW addendum and invoice term options (VertexLabs)

Thanks everyone — net-45 with a signed PO is acceptable; VertexLabs will route the PO this week to hit the first billing period in mid-October. We appreciate the inclusion of the 30-day optimization audit and the burst band mechanics. One ask: can we add a clause that caps potential surprise overage liability during the first two months after a tier uplift to 20% of the uplift month invoice (we're asking for a capped exposure window while our infra teams tune the calls)? If you can put that in the SOW I can get internal approval faster.

Assuming that piece is added, we’re good to sign and move to e-sign. Please send the final doc and DocuSign link once updated.

—Sam
Head of Platform, VertexLabs
